llm.summary: This skill is a legitimate planning workflow, but it automatically writes project files, invokes other skills and subagents, and continues into later phases without a clear approval gate.

dimensions.detail: The brainstorming purpose fits most content, but the artifact expands into mandatory War Room deliberation, automated spec review, and auto-invocation of project specification, which is broader than a simple ideation aid.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad triggers such as planning and requirements, then instructs automatic handoffs and explicitly says not to prompt for confirmation before continuing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown skill files only; static scan and VirusTotal telemetry are clean, and no executable installer or hidden install-time behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: For a brainstorming skill, automatic context sharing with other skills/subagents and automatic edits to planning documents create more environmental reach than users may expect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact directs saving a project brief to docs/project-brief.md and session details to .attune/brainstorm-session.json, which may contain sensitive project context and is not clearly opt-in.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you want a brainstorming-only assistant. Use it only when you are comfortable with it creating planning files, storing session state, sharing project context with subagents or related skills, and continuing into specification unless you explicitly stop it or use the documented standalone/skip options.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the concern: the skill advertises brainstorming but requires automatic downstream workflow continuation into other Attune phases.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Artifact evidence supports the concern: it mandates War Room invocation, passes all brainstorming context, and dispatches a review subagent before proceeding.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation terms are risky in context because activation can lead to local file writes and automatic workflow handoffs.
[SQP-2] expected: Writing a project brief is coherent with the skill's planning purpose, but saving both the brief and session state should be more clearly disclosed and user-controlled.
[EA2] unexpected: The no-confirmation instruction is materially concerning because it removes an approval checkpoint before additional skill invocation and review loops.
